newsitem.title: USA: KCS to delay stock sale, acquisition.
newsitem.headline: KCS to delay stock sale, acquisition.

text.p: KCS Energy Inc. said Monday a Texas jury ordered it to pay $143.2 million in a lawsuit filed by a Tenneco Inc. subsidiary and that it will delay a stock offering and the closing of its latest takeover.
The verdict, which caught KCS by surprise, stifled the company's growth plans and sparked a sharp sell-off of its stock.

"This is a significant development because it puts a monkey-wrench into KCS Energy's growth plans," said Chris Sheehan, an analyst at John S. Herold Inc. "The company had planned to grow its non-contract reserves and this acquisition was a step on the way."
KCS's secondary stock offering and the $217 million acquisition of MidAmerican Energy Co.'s oil and natural gas operations "may possibly be terminated," Chief Executive James Christmas said.

After a delayed opening, KCS tumbled as low as $31.625 before closing down $6.875 at $35.25 on the New York Stock Exchange. Tenneco rose 37.5 cents to $51, and MidAmerican edged up 12.5 cents to $15.375, also on the NYSE.
One analyst expected KCS shares to trade in the new, lower range until the litigation was resolved.
"We won't see any change in the share price until the situation changes materially," Sheehan said.

KCS said a jury in a civil trial in state district court in Zapata County, Texas, awarded Tenneco $143.2 million after agreeing with charges that KCS substituted natural gas sold to Tenneco from the Bob West Field in South Texas with gas that was of a lower quality than they had agreed upon.
The suit was filed by Tenneco's Tennessee Gas Pipeline Co. in April 1995.
Christmas said the independent energy company, based in Edison, N.J., planned "to file a motion to have the verdict set aside and, if necessary, to file a motion for a new trial.
"If these motions are denied, we plan to file an appeal with the Texas Court of Appeals ...," he said.

KCS said the jury's verdict, which includes about $114 million in punitive damanges, did not affected current or future sales of natural gas from wells covered by the contract with Tenneco, which runs through January 1999.
Only sales made from company-operated wells during the period in question were affected, KCS said, pointing out "the terms of the contract were upheld in previous judicial ratings favouring KCS."

"We believe that the jury's verdict was not supported by the facts and is inconsistent with applicable law. We believe we acted fully within our rights under the contract and that our (natural) gas met contract specifications," Christmas said.
He and other company officials were not available due to an analysts' telephone conference call from which reporters were excluded.
While analysts said the verdict would not likely affect operations, one said it would lower KCS's capital spending. "It will definitely make capital expenditures difficult," he said.
On Nov. 15, KCS said it agreed to buy InterCoast Oil and Gas Co., the Oklahoma-based oil and gas exploration and production subsidiary and gas marketing units of MidAmerican Energy.
On Nov. 22, the company also said it agreed to acquire 8.5 billion cubic feet equivalent of proved oil and natural gas reserves from ATP Oil & Gas Corp. for undisclosed terms.
